customManagers.description: Bump the Go tools the Makefile builds under .tools, each marked with a 'renovate:' comment on the line above its pin. Go module tags carry the v the Makefile writes, so the matched value is reused as is.

The linter version ci.yml hands the reusable lint workflow. Matched on the input's own name rather than a marker comment so the workflow file stays untouched, and grouped with the Makefile pin below so the two never disagree.

packageRules.description: A bump lands as 'chore', a type release-please-config.json hides, so it waits for the next release instead of making one. The rule below types what a release ships; the rest changes neither the binary nor the release image: an action, the tools the Makefile builds, the linter ci.yml hands the reusable workflow, mise's pin, and Dockerfile.full, whose image docker-full.yml publishes whenever the file changes and never at a release. A release made for one of them is not free either: bump-rta.yml in rta-plugins releases every plugin against each rta release.

What a release ships lands as 'build', which release-please-config.json lists under Dependencies and releases: go.mod's modules are compiled into the binary and Dockerfile builds the release image, so a bump of either reaches nobody until a release carries it.
Non-major Go module bumps land together: one commit and one patch release a week rather than one per module. A vulnerable module skips both the grouping and the schedule through the OSV alerts above.
The linter is pinned twice on purpose - the Makefile for `make lint`, ci.yml for the reusable workflow - so a finding here is a finding there. One pull request moves both.

The Go toolchain is the go directive in go.mod, which CI reads through go-version-file, the golang image both Dockerfiles build in, and the pin in mise.toml. One pull request moves all three, as 'build' whichever of them it moves: Go's runtime and standard library are compiled into the binary, so a Go security release reaches nobody until a release carries it.
A new digest under the same golang tag is the same Go release, and both Dockerfiles build with CGO off, so the binary does not change: the bump waits for a release rather than making one.

gcfg moves with go-git, never ahead of it. builtin/git reads config and includes with the reader go-git's own decoder uses, so a file one refuses the other refused already; go-git v5 requires gcfg v1, and gcfg v2 (a new import path) arrives with go-git v6, which moves both together.
Reusable workflows are called at the moving v0 major tag on purpose until github-workflows reaches v1 - don't pin or bump them.
